message:
fix(picker): a card that refuses the click should not look pressable

Follow-up to the empty-list fix, covering the two things the review asked for that the
commit before this one did not do: the contract the cards are drawn against, and a
negative control that actually fails.

begin_pc_target_selection refuses a selection when the control channel is down. The
refresh button next to the cards already drew itself disabled for that reason; the
cards did not, so on a failed connect they looked as pressable as ever and simply did
nothing. The value that says whether an action is possible was already being computed
one line above and thrown away with a (void) cast. The cards use it now.

The empty-state decision moves into a header of its own so it can be checked against a
table of states rather than only photographed, and the table is worth something only
because of the control beside it: the logic that shipped in 0.2.121 is kept in the test
and run against the same rows, where it disagrees on seven of nine. Revert the fix and
the table breaks while the control passes, which says which of the two is measuring the
change. Rendering the reverted build puts the contradictory sentence back at the same
place on the error screens and brightens the captions again, measured in pixels.

One sentence from the previous commit was simply untrue and is gone. It told the user
the window list was hidden by host configuration; the host sets that flag and then
enumerates the windows anyway. The flag means the target is fixed, which the header
already says, so a locked picker with nothing to share now says nothing extra. There is
a screenshot of that state, which there had not been.
